title: Differential entrance policies for tiered traffic with quota-aware admission and regional fallbacks
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: Free-tier bursts and unpredictable regional hotspots are causing transient congestion that impacts paid customers' latency and SLA guarantees. Current admission uses coarse plan-based queues which either over-prioritize paid traffic (wasting reserved capacity) or bluntly throttle free traffic (poor UX). Additionally, when a preferred model is unavailable we need a principled fallback sequence that preserves latency SLOs and cost targets while minimizing quality regression for each customer tier.

Goal: Implement a differential 'entrance policy' subsystem that: (1) applies quota-aware admission decisions at ingress, (2) routes requests by tier and preferred region with probabilistic smoothing to avoid thundering bursts, (3) supports prioritized fallback to cheaper/quantized model variants when higher-cost model capacity is constrained, and (4) exposes metrics and controls for SRE/PM to tune aggressiveness per release.

Scope: This ticket covers design and implementation of the ingress admission controller, regional affinity mapping, and model-variant fallback policy. It includes a canary rollout plan, dashboards, and automated tests. Autoscaler/placement changes will be tracked in dependent work.

Design notes and decisions so far: 
- Admission model: implement an admission controller at the edge that evaluates (tier, tenant_quota_remaining, regional_capacity_signal, observed_latency_headroom) to compute a score used for deterministic admission or probabilistic demotion.
- Tier semantics: three lanes — free (best-effort), paid (higher priority, burst credits), enterprise (guaranteed lanes with reservation). Enterprise lanes are allowed to preempt soft spokes only when preemption budget > 0.
- Quota handling: utilise per-tenant 'consumption window' that decays credits over a sliding window. When credits low, we apply a soft demotion (probabilistic downgrade) rather than hard reject to preserve UX.
- Regional selection: map user region -> preferred region pool; apply a spillover policy that prefers local pools but allows cross-region routing if local congestion persists beyond a configured window. Spillover is limited by egress cost budget per tenant.
- Fallback variants: define fallback chains per model family (eg. redwood-llm-v3 -> redwood-llm-v3-quant4 -> redwood-llm-compact). Fallback selection uses a quality-loss budget per tier: free can accept larger quality deltas; enterprise has tight quality budget and prefers cross-region routing before a model downgrade.
- Smoothness: to avoid oscillation, use a token-bucket-like admission with probabilistic smoothing (p = sigmoid(alpha*(credit_ratio - threshold))) and a holdout window after any demotion to prevent immediate re-admission flapping.
- Observability: emit per-request tags: admission_result, admission_reason, chosen_region, chosen_model_variant, preemption_flag. Aggregate to tenant-level metrics for SLO dashboards.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Deterministic vs probabilistic admission: deterministic rules are simpler but lead to synchronized drops when many tenants hit thresholds. Probabilistic smoothing reduces spikes but complicates debugging. We prefer probabilistic with strong telemetry.
- Cross-region vs model-downgrade: cross-region maintains model quality but may increase latency/egress cost. Default: prefer regional spillover for enterprise/paid until latency degradation surpasses bound, then fallback to a lower-cost model variant.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Admission controller deployed to canary region and handling 1000rps simulated traffic with mixed tiers without regression in paid P95 latency > 10% vs baseline.
- Per-tenant quota enforcement matches spec (credits decay window behaves correctly under tests).
- Fallback chain respects per-tier quality budgets in integration tests (synthetic prompts scored against reference outputs).
- Dashboards: tenant-level admission outcomes, fallback rates, region spillover counts, latency per tier.
- Automated chaos test: when primary region pool is artificially limited, paid and enterprise traffic see expected spillover/downgrade behavior per config.

Rollout plan: 
1) Unit + integration tests + simulated load (PR) -> code review.
2) Canary rollout in a single region with 5% of traffic using feature flag. Monitor metrics for 48h.
3) Expand to multi-region canary (select low-risk tenant cohort) and run E2E quality checks.
4) Default enable for all tenants with monitoring alarms and automatic rollback if enterprise P95 SLA > configured threshold.

Open questions: 
- How to expose admin controls for non-engineering teams? (suggest Console feature toggles per tenant).
- Exact decay window and alpha parameters for smoothing — propose we A/B test two configurations.
- Billing implications for cross-region spillover — need PM/legal input.

Related artifacts: design doc (Confluence), model-family fallback registry, billing policy draft.
